tool.name: BatchClipByFeatureClass
tool.displayname: Batch Clip to Each Feature Class

param.name: clip_workspace
param.dialogReference: The geodatabase or folder that holds the polygon feature classes to clip to. The tool runs once for each polygon feature class at the top level of this workspace (feature datasets are not searched). Point and line feature classes are skipped.

param.name: wildcard
param.dialogReference: Limits the feature classes by name. Use * for any characters, for example County* . The default * uses every polygon feature class.

param.name: in_layer
param.dialogReference: The features or raster to clip. Features are clipped with Pairwise Clip; a raster is clipped with Clip Raster using the polygon as the clipping geometry.

param.name: out_workspace
param.dialogReference: The geodatabase or folder where the clipped outputs are written. Existing outputs with the same name are overwritten if the geoprocessing option to overwrite is on.

param.name: name_template
param.dialogReference: The output name. {Name} is replaced by the current feature class name and {n} by the 0-based iteration number, for example {Name}_clip gives Monroe_County_clip. They play the part of ModelBuilder's %Name% and %n% inline variables; the % form cannot be used in a script tool because geoprocessing replaces %n% before the tool runs.

param.name: out_datasets
param.dialogReference: All clipped outputs, one per feature class, collected into one list (like Collect Values in ModelBuilder).

tool.summary: Clips one input layer to every polygon feature class in a workspace and names each output from a template. It is the script-tool twin of a ModelBuilder model that uses Iterate Feature Classes, the %Name% inline variable and Collect Values.
tool.usage:
• Keep only the clip polygons in the clip workspace; every polygon feature class there is used.

  • Feature classes are processed in name order. The messages list each output, its size and the time it took.

  • A template without {Name} or {n} raises a warning, because every iteration would write the same output.
